item.title: Nigeria-Indonesia investment to boost GDP, create jobs, says NICCI president, Balogun
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The President of the Nigerian Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, NICCI, Ishmael Balogun, has said increased investment between Nigeria and Indonesia, particularly in oil and gas exploration, will boost Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, create jobs and promote knowledge transfer. Balogun spoke during the Nigerian Indonesian Investment and Trade Forum, NIITF, which held its fifth edition in Jakarta from October 20 to 21, 2026, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment in oil and gas, renewable energy, agriculture, pharmaceuticals and infrastructure development. He said stronger economic cooperation between the two countries would enable Nigerian businesses to access more opportunities in Indonesia while attracting foreign direct investment into Nigeria. He cited the chamber’s engagements during Food and Beverage West Africa in Lagos and the Kano Indonesian Expo, where Indonesian companies were invited to meet Nigerian businesses and explore commercial partnerships. He said the chamber had also recorded increased participation by Nigerian businesses at the Indonesian Trade Expo, adding that 150 visitor visas were issued by the Indonesian Embassy in Nigeria for the Nigerian delegation to participate in this year’s activities. Balogun maintained that the chamber was committed to strengthening business relations in both directions by helping Nigerian companies explore Indonesia and encouraging Indonesian companies to establish partnerships and investments in Nigeria. item.title: 2027: Enugu ADC alleges attacks, demands level playing field
item.description: By Anayo Okoli The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Enugu State has called on the state government to ensure a level playing field for all political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, alleging attacks on opposition supporters and urging authorities to prevent political violence. The party’s governorship candidate, Ocho Obodoeze, made the call after receiving an award from the Correspondents Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Enugu State Council. Obodoeze accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of suppressing opposition parties and urged the state government to allow all political parties to campaign freely in accordance with the law. He also called on the government to fulfil its responsibility of protecting lives and property amid concerns over reported political violence in the state. “Enugu State Government should allow every political party to campaign in the state, in line with the Electoral Act and guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the 2027 general election. “The government should desist from muzzling opposition parties. Instead, they should allow them to campaign freely like the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is doing. Election is not a do-or-die affair. The will of the people must be allowed to prevail,” he said. Obodoeze dedicated his award to Ifeanyi Christopher Nworie, who reportedly died from gunshot injuries allegedly sustained during an attack on supporters of the opposition New Democratic Congress (NDC). Describing the gesture as emotional, the ADC candidate recalled that Nworie died from injuries he sustained during an attack by gunmen on an opposition party’s campaign office in Enugu on October 10, 2026. He alleged that the incident reflected a pattern of attacks against opposition parties since political activities began ahead of the 2027 elections. The Enugu State Government, however, has denied involvement in political attacks in the state, insisting that opposition parties are free to campaign and criticise Governor Peter Mbah’s administration. Meanwhile, the Enugu State chapter of the ADC has congratulated Obodoeze on the award presented to him during the Correspondents Chapel’s 2026 Press Week celebration. He also promised supporters prosperity if re-elected, assuring them that they would not regret giving him a second term. “You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you for that, to seek your mandate for the second term, to keep a promise on prosperity, continuity and progress. I have an argument, I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did! They created hunger, they created poverty, we are trying to eradicate it,” he said. “We pay salaries regularly, our governors are working, I am proud of them, they are developing. I hear my opponent talking about hunger, poverty. Who created it? They did! They created the hunger, they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said. He also defended his administration’s record on salary payments and commended state governors for their performance, saying they were making progress in their respective states. “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing,” Tinubu said. The president thanked Kaduna residents for supporting him in the previous presidential election, saying their votes contributed to his emergence as president. “You gave me joy to remember the victory you gave me to become president. I come again to thank you,” he said. Tinubu appealed to Nigerians to give him another term, saying he wanted to sustain his promises of prosperity, continuity, progress and development. item.title: EPL: Arsenal see off Everton, go joint-top after Man City defeat
item.description: Manchester City’s flawless start to the Premier League season was ended in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa on Saturday that allowed Arsenal to join them at the top of the table with victory over Everton. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. Nicolas Jackson struck twice for Unai Emery’s men to continue a fine run of form for a new-look Villa side. Erling Haaland briefly levelled early in the second half, but Maresca was left to rue City not making more of their dominance for large spells of the game. “We lost because we probably are not being clinical enough in their box,” said Maresca. The Villa side that won the Europa League last season was decimated by high-profile departures during the transfer window. But Emery has quickly moulded his new squad into shape with Jackson proving his critics from a difficult spell at Chelsea wrong. The Senegal international pounced on an error by Marc Guehi to fire Villa ahead after just six minutes. Another of Villa’s new signings Zion Suzuki then thwarted City with a string of stunning saves. Haaland headed in his 13th goal in 10 games this season to equalise. Villa, though, swiftly responded as Gianluigi Donnarumma failed to keep out Jackson’s low shot on the hour mark. “A fantastic day to share with our supporters in Villa Park,” said Emery. “We felt that this is our fortress and the energy the supporters gave us was really fantastic.” – Arsenal’s set-piece prowess – Arsenal took advantage to move alongside City on 21 points from eight games with a routine 2-0 win against Everton. Shorn of the creative inspiration of Bukayo Saka, who is set for a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a thigh injury, Arsenal had to rely on their set-piece prowess to get the job done. Ezri Konsa bundled in his first goal for the club after Everton failed to clear a corner to open the scoring on seven minutes. Fellow centre-back Gabriel Magalhaes doubled the lead for Mikel Arteta’s men midway through the second period. Fulham further eased the pressure on manager Alvaro Arbeloa with a 1-0 win at Coventry thanks to Oscar Bobb’s individual effort. A second consecutive victory propels the Cottagers out of the relegation zone and up to 12th. Tottenham are also seeking to escape the bottom three when they travel to Chelsea in the evening kick-off, aiming to improve on a terrible record at Stamford Bridge. On Sunday the focus turns on Manchester United boss Michael Carrick when his side take on Bournemouth. A seven-game winless streak has plunged Carrick’s future into doubt just months after he was hired on a two-year deal after a successful interim spell in charge at the end of last season. item.title: Como follow Man Utd thumping with victory in Serie A
item.description: Como backed up their brilliant Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in a 2-0 Serie A win against Sassuolo on Saturday. Cesc Fabregas’s side climbed to fourth in the table, just two points adrift of early leaders Inter Milan who host Fiorentina on Sunday. Como were frustrated for long periods by a stubborn Sassuolo team, but clinched an ultimately comfortable win courtesy of Douvikas’s two goals in the space of 11 second-half minutes. The Greece striker has now scored five goals in his last four games, and eight in all competitions in total this season. Como, who qualified for Europe for the first time in their history last term, thrashed Man United 4-1 in the Champions League in midweek. Later Saturday, Roma bid to go top of the table when they visit Napoli, before second-placed Lazio also eye the summit in their home game against Parma. He said the failure to construct the proposed Ubani–Agbo–Umueze Road had continued to expose road users to the dangers of the busy Umuahia–Uzuakoli Road. ” In 2013 when we were asked to relocate to this place, Government promised to build a shorter route to the market passing through Umueze and Agbo to make it easily accessible from the city but up till today we have not seen it. The other day, a trader was returning to the City after the day’s sales and boarded a tricycle. On their way through the busy Uzuakoli road, a trailer had a break failure and rammed into the Keke. The head of the woman was cut off immediately as a result of the impact. This is affecting the few of us that are here. ” This is 13 years we were forced to come here but this market does not look as if it has lasted for six months because it is going down everyday.” Beyond the physical deterioration, Okeke said the absence of banks in and around the market had created security risks for traders who handle cash from daily sales. Although we pay, we don’t yet see anything they are doing with it. ” I’m not sure the Governor is aware of this. That’s why I’m appealing to him to look into what is happening at Ubani Ultra-modern Market. We are suffering here. We are just merely surviving by God’s grace. There is no future for this market as long as the same Government continues to allow some traders return to Isigate. We heard that revenue collectors collect revenues from the traders there twice a day. That’s why they are not serious about forcing them out of that place. We are the ones suffering it here”. ‘Our business capital is depreciating’ A patent medicine dealer, Mr Michael Ubani, said the market’s fortunes would continue to decline unless the government enforced its relocation policy and addressed the infrastructure deficit. He said traders who obeyed the relocation directive had been left to bear the consequences while competing markets continued to operate within the city centre. ” We are hopelessly struggling to survive here. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.

item.title: Tinubu, Shettima flag off APC 2027 campaign in Kaduna
item.description: President Bola Tinubu arrived in Kaduna State on Saturday ahead of the flag-off of the All Progressives Congress’ 2027 presidential campaign, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana, also arriving for the event. APC National Chairman, Prof Nentawe Yilwatda, the Director-General of the presidential campaign, Abdul’aziz Yari, and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani were at the airport to welcome the President. Shettima’s arrival was announced in a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha. Mr Nkwocha said APC governors, party leaders, elected officials, political stakeholders and supporters were gathering at the Kaduna Township Stadium for the commencement of the party’s nationwide presidential campaign. He described the event as a significant moment for Kaduna, noting that the city would serve as the launching point for the APC’s campaign ahead of the 2027 presidential election. According to the statement, the campaign would provide the ruling party with an opportunity to present its “Renewed Hope 2.0” agenda and highlight the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “The stage is set. Kaduna is ready. The 2027 campaign begins!” the statement read in part. It added, “Asiwaju is here. Northwest for the takeaway!” Ahead of the President’s arrival, security operatives on Saturday barricaded strategic locations across Kaduna metropolis as authorities stepped up security preparations for the campaign event. Personnel from the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services, Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Nigeria Immigration Service and the Kaduna State Vigilance Service were deployed to different parts of the city. The security personnel were stationed at major roundabouts and along roads leading to the venue of the campaign flag-off. Muhammadu Buhari Way, formerly known as WAFF Road, was blocked by security operatives ahead of the expected movement of the President and his entourage through the route. The Ahmadu Bello Stadium roundabout was also manned by heavily armed soldiers, police officers and plain-clothes security personnel. The security restrictions affected traffic in several parts of Kaduna, triggering a gridlock that extended from Junction Road to Ahmadu Bello Way. item.title: French Montana, Jorja Smith to perform at Ballon d’Or 2026
item.description: Ballon d’Or organisers revealed on Saturday that star US rapper French Montana and English singer Jorja Smith would perform at this year’s ceremony, part of efforts to draw more viewers to the awards event. Last year saw Canadian singer Charlotte Cardin do her best to lift the somewhat stiff atmosphere at the prize giving in Paris as she performed her hit “Feel Good” in front of a motionless crowd of suited footballers and VIPs at a theatre. The most prestigious individual award in football will be handed out in London next Monday, with Kylian Mbappe, Spanish pair Lamine Yamal and Ferran Torres, PSG duo Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Harry Kane all seen as frontrunners. It is the first time the Ballon d’Or ceremony, now in its 70th edition, will be hosted in Britain. French Montana has over 30 million monthly listeners on Spotify, mixing Moroccan influences, trap, afrobeat and New York hip hop culture. He has collaborated on hits with Drake, Cardi B and Swae Lee, with whom he made the 2017 track “Unforgettable”, which has racked up 1.9 billion views on YouTube. English singer-songwriter Jorja Smith mixes RnB, soul and jazz influences, drawing on her Jamaican heritage and her classical music training. Her career took off 10 years ago with “Blue Lights”, followed by other tracks ranging from intimate to more danceable. In addition to their “exclusive performances” during the evening, “other surprises are planned”, the Groupe L’Equipe, which organises the ceremony, said in a statement sent to AFP. The group owns the magazine France Football, which has been awarding the Ballon d’Or since 1956. It is based on voting by a jury of journalists from the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings. In 2025, the top male player prize was awarded to France’s Ousmane Dembele and the women’s to Spain’s Aitana Bonmati. The ceremony will be broadcast on sports streaming website DAZN, and the L’Equipe TV channel in France. It will be hosted by former France and Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, and sports journalist Kate Scott. In 2022, tenor Andrea Bocelli was chosen to open the ceremony. item.title: Man City beaten by Aston Villa to end perfect Premier League start
item.description: Manchester City’s perfect Premier League start came to a crashing halt in a 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa as Nicolas Jackson’s double extended an upturn in form for Unai Emery’s new-look side. Enzo Maresca had become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club but failed to find a solution to City’s struggles at Villa Park, where they have now lost for the past four seasons. After Jackson blasted home the opener after just six minutes, Villa relied on a brilliant goalkeeping display from Zion Suzuki to keep City at bay. Erling Haaland breifly levelled early in the second half only for Villa to respond on the hour mark when Jackson drilled home Ibrahim Mbaye’s cross. Four years on from Emery’s arrival, which has transformed the club from a sleeping giant into the Champions League, the Spaniard is working more magic despite seeing the spine of his squad in recent seasons decimated. Six of the side that started Villa’s victory in last season’s Europa League left during the transfer window. But the recruitment of the likes of Jackson, Suzuki, Mbaye and Johan Manzambi is already paying dividends after a slow start to the campaign. Until now City have managed to shrug off the cloud hanging over the club’s Premier League future to keep winning on the field. The 10-time English champions are appealing a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018 that could lead to swingeing sanctions, including relegation. There was little sign of that distraction affecting Enzo Maresca’s men, but they were made to pay for two sloppy defensive errors. A heavy touch by Marc Guehi presented Jackson with possession for the opening goal as he cut inside Elliott Anderson and blasted high past Gianluigi Donnarumma. City largely dominated the remainder of the first half, but could not find a way past Suzuki. Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Abdukodir Khusanov were all denied before Ndiaye struck the post. City’s pressure finally told on 52 minutes when Haaland powered in a header from Ndiaye’s cross for his 13th goal in 10 appearances this season. Josko Gvardiol nearly completed the comeback when Suzuki turned his blistering drive into the crossbar moments later. Instead, it was Villa to got the decisive third goal. Mbaye was played in behind the City defence and from his cross, Jackson’s low effort should have been saved by Donnarumma. The visitors pressed in vain for another equaliser to allow Arsenal the chance to move level on points at the top of the table when they host Everton later on Saturday. item.title: 2027: Atiku is North’s enemy, says Akume
item.description: ….Says, power rotation agreed in Kaduna to keep Nigeria one By Omeiza Ajayi, Kaduna As the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) flagged off its presidential campaign on Saturday in Kaduna, Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, declared that any northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the region. Former vice president Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress ADC is the only prominent northern politician seeking to wrestle power from incumbent President Bola Tinubu in the next year’s presidential contest. This was as he reminded Northerners that the agreement on power rotation between the North and the South was reached in Kaduna State to keep the country together. His spokesman, Yomi Odunuga, in a statement on Saturday, said the SGF spoke at a pre-campaign meeting with a large crowd of Benue State indigenes residing in Kaduna. “Remember that it was in this same Kaduna State that we agreed on power rotation between the North and the South. You cannot doubt the credentials of those that reached this agreement at that time, and it was done to keep this country together. We agreed on power shift, and that is what has kept this country going. That is what has retained our territorial integrity,” Akume said. On that basis, he declared that any Northerner seeking to contest the 2027 presidential election is an enemy of the North, insisting that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains the right candidate to lead Nigeria beyond 2027. “Anybody who is from the North and running for the presidency is an enemy of the North. Don’t allow that pretender to deceive you. It is not yet our turn. The North’s turn is in 2031. Prepare to vote for Tinubu. Do not allow anyone to destroy the country because of a vaunting personal ambition,” he said. The SGF urged the North to back Tinubu’s re-election bid and wait until 2031 before seeking to return to the presidency. item.title: Thousands March In France Against Far-Right Party Congress
item.description: Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched in the French city of Orléans Saturday against a congress by far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party there, AFP journalists saw. The protest — held on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living after ones a week ago that devolved into street violence — criticised both Le Pen and centrist President Emmanuel Macron. France’s President Emmanuel Macron meets with elected officials at the town hall following a shooting in Trappes, near Paris, on October 23, 2026. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled, while carrying placards that read “The Youth say ‘screw you’ to the National Rally” and “Hotter than fascists”. The two-day RN congress in Orleans was the first big party campaign rally by Le Pen, whom surveys put as the leading candidate to succeed Macron in presidential elections in six months. But registered voters are not actual votes, political endorsements are not public opinion, and the North is not a single electoral personality. That is the political signal this week. Why Kaduna matters Kaduna is in the North-West region. Kaduna is an appropriate starting point because it captures both the opportunity and the danger confronting Tinubu. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. The state also embodies several issues that could determine northern voting behaviour: insecurity, rural poverty, food prices, religious sensitivity and the relationship between elite political agreements and popular sentiment. By beginning there, the APC is signalling that it will not concede the region to Atiku merely because he is a northern Muslim. It is relying on Vice-President Kashim Shettima, governors, ministers, traditional relationships and a greatly expanded party structure to offset Atiku’s regional appeal. That structure matters. The APC now enjoys an extraordinary advantage in the number of governors, lawmakers and local political networks under its control. Governors influence campaign financing, mobilisation and the organisation required to convert public sympathy into votes. The party’s challenge is that political machinery can mobilise supporters, but it cannot permanently insulate an incumbent from lived economic experience. The contest between structure and hardship The APC’s campaign argument will be that the most painful period of reform has passed. Inflation has moderated, foreign reserves have improved, economic growth has strengthened, and the Central Bank has begun adjusting interest rates. The administration will argue that removing the petrol subsidy and reforming the foreign-exchange market prevented a deeper fiscal crisis. The opposition’s reply is more immediate: food, transport, energy and business costs remain painfully high. That explains the political significance of the National Economic Council’s newly approved 90-day action plan. It prioritises food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. It also proposes a national dashboard to track projects and the use of savings from subsidy removal. On paper, these are reasonable interventions. The problem is timing. The presidential election is 86 days away, while the relief plan is designed to run for 90 days. Atiku’s campaign has therefore called it “election bait,” arguing that Nigerians are being asked to vote before the promised relief can be fully assessed. That is a partisan allegation, not proof that the programme is improper. But the calendar gives the criticism political force. The government can answer it only through early, measurable delivery. What food has become cheaper? Which households have received support? What projects have been completed? How much has been spent, by whom and under what criteria? Announcements will not be sufficient. The electorate needs receipts. The opposition’s unity problem While the APC prepares a major campaign launch, opposition parties are again discussing a consensus candidate. Representatives of the ADC, NDC, PRP, SDP, APM and PDP have inaugurated legal and media committees to develop a framework for cooperation. Atiku, Peter Obi, Donald Duke and Adewale Adebayo are among the names mentioned in the talks. Coalition organisers say negotiations are progressing towards a single candidate. That claim should be treated cautiously. The Independent National Electoral Commission has already published 18 presidential candidates, including Atiku for the ADC and Obi for the NDC. Agreeing that the opposition should unite is therefore much easier than determining who withdraws, who leads, what happens to the running mates and how supporters are transferred between parties. There is also no guarantee that voters will follow elite instructions. An Atiku endorsement of Obi would not automatically deliver Atiku’s northern vote. An Obi endorsement of Atiku would not automatically transfer younger urban voters or the South-East. Nigerian politicians often mistake negotiations among leaders for consolidation among electorates. The opposition nevertheless understands the arithmetic. Tinubu won in 2023 with 36.61 per cent of the valid votes; 8.79 million votes. Atiku and Obi together received more than 13 million. That does not mean a joint ticket would have automatically defeated Tinubu, because elections are shaped by turnout, geography and the constitutional requirement for national spread. But it shows why fragmentation remains the APC’s quiet ally. Unless the coalition produces a credible agreement quickly, it risks becoming a committee for managing defeat. The register question The emphasis on 103.43 million voters has also reopened an important transparency dispute. INEC says the total follows the addition of approximately 10.77 million new registrants. Atiku has demanded that the preliminary register be made available for public inspection, alleging that an online page intended for that purpose was empty. The allegation does not establish manipulation. Technical delays or publication problems are not evidence of a compromised register. But INEC should resolve the issue immediately. A national figure cannot substitute for a register that citizens and parties can scrutinise. The public must be able to identify duplicate entries, deceased persons, omissions and questionable registrations before the final roll is certified. If parties are already building campaign strategies around precise regional totals, voters deserve access to the underlying data. First, watch the language and attendance at Saturday’s Kaduna rally. A large gathering will demonstrate organisational capacity, but the more important question is whether influential northern leaders offer genuine commitments or merely perform ceremonial loyalty. Second, watch whether the 90-day economic plan produces identifiable benefits before election day. Its political credibility will depend on outcomes, not intentions. Third, watch the opposition negotiations. A consensus announced after ballots and campaign loyalties have hardened may be largely symbolic. Finally, watch INEC. Publication and scrutiny of the voter register will be an early test of whether the Commission intends to manage doubts proactively or react only after they become political crises. The APC is campaigning on structure and patience. The opposition is campaigning on hardship and change, but without yet agreeing on whose change. item.description: Hundreds of protests were held in France Saturday as nationwide anger grows over the cost of living, with security forces massing to prevent a repeat of violence that marred demonstrations last week. Here are the latest developments: – ‘Calm’ in Paris – French police had arrested 135 people nationwide and seized a variety of weapons, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said, adding that, so far, “there has been no major incident”. Weapons confiscated included metal balls, lead pellets, fireworks, slingshots, steel balls, improvised weapons, a katana and airsoft weapons, he said. Paris police described the situation as “calm” at midday. – ‘Scandalous’ – Hundreds of demonstrators could be seen gathering at Porte d’Italie in Paris, where authorities have said they must begin the only authorised march. Union representative Murielle Guilbert told reporters it was “scandalous” that President Emmanuel Macron had forbidden protesters from demonstrating “where we wish to demonstrate”. “We are here today, quite obviously, because there is immense social anger in this country, and because wages have still not been increased to the level they should be,” she added. Paris police at the last minute ordered the union-organised march be moved from Bastille, in the centre, to the more remote Porte d’Italie on the southeastern rim. Unions said they reluctantly agreed. But the Yellow Vests — a loosely organised group that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated they would not comply. – Halloween protests called – One group organising Saturday’s demonstrations — the Yellow Vests — said they would hold another round of protests on October 31. Organisers called for rallies and a sit-in outside parliament and city halls nationwide, condemning the “authoritarian drift” of President Emmanuel Macron’s government and urging citizens to stand up for “public freedoms”. – Tear gas in Lyon – Police fired teargas to disperse some 150 people protesting in the southeastern city of Lyon, in an area banned to all demonstrations, an AFP journalist saw. Police fired several teargas grenades to clear the group near a university faculty and the city’s police station as part of nationwide rallies against the cost of living. The protest criticised both leading presidential candidate Le Pen and centrist Macron. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. – Louvre, Orsay closed – The Louvre, d’Orsay, and Picasso museums, as well as the Grand Palais in Paris, were closed Saturday. The culture ministry had called on institutions to take every measure to ensure the safety of visitors and staff, and the protection of artworks. A country that ranks highly in one category may occupy a lower position in another, highlighting the different priorities and capabilities of armed forces worldwide. Japan’s 2026 defence white paper also highlights the security challenges surrounding the Korean Peninsula and the military capabilities maintained by North Korea. Tank Ranks by Country China leads the ranking of countries with the largest tank inventories, followed by Russia, while North Korea occupies third place ahead of the United States. The figures illustrate the importance several countries continue to place on land-based military operations, although the number of tanks alone does not determine the effectiveness of an armoured force. Russia has 5,870 tanks, while China follows closely with 5,630. North Korea ranks third with 4,895 tanks, ahead of the United States, which has 4,666. India occupies fifth place with 3,913 tanks, followed by Egypt with 3,620. Pakistan ranks seventh with 2,677, while Iran is eighth with 2,675. Türkiye takes ninth place with 2,284 tanks, and Vietnam rounds out the top 10 with 1,999. North Korea’s extensive tank inventory reflects its long-standing focus on conventional ground warfare. Research published by the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) indicates that the country operates a combination of older Soviet-inspired designs and newer equipment. Maintaining a large number of tanks can provide a military with substantial ground-firepower capacity. However, the age and technological sophistication of the vehicles also matter. Modern armour, targeting systems, sensors, weapons and battlefield communications can significantly affect the performance of tanks in combat. Consequently, a country with a larger inventory does not necessarily possess a more effective armoured force than one with fewer but more advanced vehicles. Military Aircraft The United States has the world’s largest military aircraft inventory, with 13,032 aircraft, placing it far ahead of other countries. Its fleet is more than three times the size of Russia’s and exceeds the combined totals of the next four countries in the ranking. Russia comes second with 4,237 military aircraft, followed by China with 3,529. India ranks fourth with 2,183, while South Korea occupies fifth place with 1,540. Pakistan follows with 1,429 aircraft, ahead of Japan, which has 1,397. Türkiye ranks eighth with 1,101, while Egypt has 1,088. France completes the top 10 with 974 military aircraft. The ranking includes aircraft across military branches, covering helicopters, transport planes, training aircraft and other military aviation assets, rather than combat jets alone. The United States’ substantial advantage reflects the requirements of maintaining military operations across multiple regions of the world. Its armed forces need to transport troops, equipment and supplies over long distances while supporting combat missions far from home bases. These operations depend on a broad aviation network that includes cargo aircraft, aerial refuelling tankers, helicopters and fighter jets. The ability to transport personnel and equipment and keep aircraft supplied with fuel is essential to sustaining military operations overseas. However, the difference between the United States and China becomes smaller when the comparison is restricted to fighter and interceptor aircraft. The United States has 1,791 fighters and interceptors, compared with China’s 1,443. This gives Washington an advantage of approximately 24 per cent in this category. The narrower gap demonstrates that the United States’ lead in total military aircraft is partly attributable to the size and diversity of its wider aviation fleet, rather than fighter aircraft alone. Naval Assets China has the world’s largest navy by the number of vessels in the Global Firepower ranking, with 841 naval assets. The United States follows with 465, while Russia ranks third with 343. The ranking reflects China’s expanding maritime capabilities and its extensive shipbuilding industry. Research by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) has examined how China’s commercial shipbuilding infrastructure can also support military ship production, providing an industrial foundation for expanding its naval fleet. North Korea ranks fourth with 338 naval assets, followed by Sweden with 332. Indonesia occupies sixth place with 304 vessels, while Italy ranks seventh with 285. India is eighth with 279 naval assets, Thailand ranks ninth with 275, and Sri Lanka completes the top 10 with 275 vessels. China’s total of 841 vessels is substantially higher than the United States’ 465, but vessel counts provide only one measure of naval strength. The figures include different types of vessels, ranging from small patrol boats and coastal craft to larger warships. Each vessel contributes one unit to the total, regardless of its size, armament or operational role. As a result, a country with numerous smaller vessels may rank above another whose fleet contains fewer but significantly larger and more capable ships. The ranking changes when naval strength is measured by total fleet tonnage instead of vessel numbers. Under Global Firepower’s fleet-tonnage ranking, the United States takes first place, with approximately 2.6 times China’s total displacement. Fleet tonnage measures the combined displacement of a navy’s vessels and provides a different perspective on the scale of its maritime assets. Nevertheless, tonnage also has limitations. It does not independently measure a vessel’s weapons, technological sophistication, operational readiness or combat effectiveness. Taken together, the rankings demonstrate why military strength cannot be assessed through a single measure. Personnel numbers reveal the size of a country’s active force, tank inventories highlight its armoured capabilities, aircraft totals reflect its aviation resources, and naval counts offer insight into its maritime presence. However, equipment quality, training, logistics, technology and the ability to deploy forces effectively are also crucial to determining a military’s overall strength. item.title: Which countries are best at maths? See top 10
item.description: China leads the world in mathematics performance among 15-year-old students, followed by Singapore and Macao, according to the latest Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results published in September 2026. The ranking compares the average mathematics scores of students across participating countries and economies. PISA assesses more than the ability to memorise formulas, examining how well students apply mathematical knowledge and reasoning to real-world problems. item.title: FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football’s governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”. But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. “I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. “But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. “I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.” No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18.
